sections.html:
Three choices face a seller in Superior: hire an agent, manage the sale alone, or deal with a cash buyer who accepts every flaw. Three things settle it: what the house needs, how fast you must move, and the net you need at the end.

Up here a buyer's inspector heads straight for the roof, the siding and the heating system. Finish that work first and a listing may reward you. Cash fits an heir, an owner living elsewhere, or anyone who cannot pay for a new roof, siding or furnace. Compare what each route leaves you after repairs, taxes and months of upkeep come off the price.

  • Listing: a bigger audience, more hoops, and weeks on the buyer's lender and inspector.
  • Sale by owner: you name the price and carry the paperwork, condition report included.
  • Cash buyer: one as-is number and a written closing date.

sections.h2: What Superior's housing market looks like
sections.html: Superior is the Douglas County seat, at the western tip of Lake Superior, and it forms the Twin Ports with Duluth, Minnesota. Owners live in 60.6 percent of housing units, and the Census median value of an owner-occupied home is $180,400. The city had an estimated 26,397 people in 2025, 1.3 percent fewer than at the 2020 base, and nearly 18 percent are 65 or older. Superior counts 11,956 households, with median rent at $900 and median household income at $64,216. Where your house falls against that midpoint depends on its condition and its street.

Superior winters are severe. Heat loss, ice and snow load are the first things an inspector checks, so gather furnace service tickets, insulation work and any roof or siding invoices.

The city's property standards require heating equipment that holds 68 degrees in habitable rooms and a water heater that supplies 120-degree water at sinks, tubs and showers. Confirm both work before an appraiser or inspector visits.

sections.h2: Which city code items should I fix before selling?
sections.html:
The building inspection office publishes a list of the most commonly violated regulations. It is written for rental owners, but most items also apply to one- and two-family homes that owners live in. Go through them before listing.

  • Address numbers readable from the street day and night.
  • A tight roof with no missing or badly worn shingles, and siding in sound, weathertight condition.
  • Stairs, porches and decks in sound repair, with graspable handrails on stairs of more than three risers.
  • Smoke alarms in each sleeping room, the access area and on each story and in the basement, plus carbon monoxide alarms where state law requires them.
  • Locks on every window within 8 feet of grade.
  • Downspouts and roof drains that connect to the city sanitary sewer must be disconnected and run outside. Contact the Environmental Services Division at 715-394-5826.

Lead-safe work practices are required when painted surfaces are disturbed. Call Building Inspection at 715-395-7288 to ask which permits are on file. The city also runs an online records search covering permits, building inspections and code compliance cases from June 2021 forward.

A seller of a building with four units or fewer owes a completed condition report to the buyer, and Chapter 709 sets the deadline at 10 days after the contract is accepted. If it comes late, the buyer has 2 business days to rescind. For any entry in their field, the owner may substitute written information from an engineer, surveyor, pest control operator, qualified third party or contractor.

The seller pays a transfer fee to the state, 30 cents per $100, set out in section 77.22. A city or county cannot tack on a separate fee where the state fee is exempt.

sections.h2: Recording at the Douglas County Register of Deeds
sections.html: Find the Douglas County Register of Deeds at 1313 Belknap Street, Room 108, in Superior, or call 715-395-1463. Recording a document costs $30 on the county's fee schedule. After a deed is recorded, check with the Real Property Lister that the tax records picked up the right owner and legal description.

sections.h2: Property taxes and a Superior sale
sections.html:
The city treasurer sends tax bills in mid to late December, and a seller should know the schedule well because it affects the closing split. The bill can be paid whole or in two parts.

Payment optionDue dateIf missed
Full payment or first installmentJanuary 31July option is lost; interest of 1 percent per month runs on the whole balance from February 1
Second installmentJuly 31Available only when the first installment was paid on time

The Lottery and Gaming Credit goes only to a primary residence, so rental or other properties do not qualify.

Delinquent taxes matter before a sale. Under state law the county may take a tax deed after two years, though its current practice is a four-year cycle, and that could change. The Douglas County Treasurer can quote a payoff if back taxes are owed. Have the number in hand before you agree to an offer, so your comparison uses the real net. The title company then settles the balance out of your proceeds at closing.

A cash buyer may be able to close before a tax deed becomes a danger, and that is a real reason owners behind on taxes look at that route. Even so, the written offer needs to say who pays the back taxes and recording costs, with the closing date spelled out.

sections.h2: Getting a Superior house ready to show
sections.html:
Lake Superior winters leave marks, so give the buyer proof the house was cared for. Pull furnace tickets, insulation receipts and roof or siding invoices into one folder. Try the smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, look at the window locks, and see whether the address numbers show from the street after dark.

If downspouts tie into the sewer, disconnect them and run them outside as the city requires, and keep the call to the Environmental Services Division on your list. An inspector who finds nothing to flag makes a buyer's lender more comfortable, and it leaves less room for a price cut late in the deal.

sections.h2: From contract to closing in Superior
sections.html: Accepting an offer starts the report deadline, so finish the form early. Gather furnace and roof records, permit answers from Building Inspection, and a payoff figure for any loan or tax balance. In the same period the title company searches the record, drafts the deed and files the transfer return online. Closing is where you sign, and the deed then goes on record at the register's office.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Superior house that has code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer takes the house as it is. A listing buyer may ask for repairs. Ask Building Inspection at 715-395-7288 whether any notice is open on the address, and answer the condition report honestly about known defects.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer fee on a Superior home sale?
faqs.a: Sellers pay 30 cents on each $100 of value. Douglas County's register takes it at recording once the electronic return is filed.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Douglas County?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars on the county schedule, with the transfer fee on top. Phone 715-395-1463 to confirm the total before anything goes in the mail.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Superior?
faqs.a: Pay everything or the first installment by January 31. The second installment comes due July 31. If January 31 is missed, interest of 1 percent a month starts February 1 and applies to the whole balance.

faqs.q: Does the seller owe the buyer a condition report in Superior?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Chapter 709 gives you 10 days from contract acceptance, and a buyer who gets it late can cancel within 2 business days. Representatives and trustees who never lived there are excused.
